term_glossary.tooltip: Electrical separation of circuits without a direct conductive path between them. Confirm the actual equipment topology and evaluated boundary.
Source capacity arranged with one additional unit beyond the units needed for the stated load. It does not establish an independent distribution path.
A designation used to identify a system voltage family; it does not describe every actual operating or transient condition.
A voltage value assigned to equipment under specified conditions. Read it together with the relevant duty and application limits.
The ability to continue the required operation during a defined electrical disturbance, for a specified duration and set of conditions.
A DC arrangement with positive and negative poles about a midpoint. Actual load connections and midpoint distribution depend on the configuration.
The conductor associated with the midpoint of a bipolar system. When distributed, it can carry normal load current from unequal pole loading.
The protective bonding function associated with earth, distinct from the conductor intended to carry normal load-return current.
An arrangement whose live system is insulated from earth or connected through impedance. Monitoring, capacitance and fault response remain important.
Energy supplied into a circuit from a connected load-side or alternate source, including stored energy that can contribute to a fault.
Coordination that disconnects the intended faulted part of a system while preserving the intended service in healthy parts.
A load’s ability to continue operating during a supply interruption or dip using its available stored energy, within defined limits.
The electrical connection boundary used for the applicable grid-interface assessment. Confirm the boundary defined by the governing requirement.
A converter that actively regulates relevant electrical behavior within its designed operating range; isolation and fault response are separate properties.
Equipment that circulates and controls coolant supplied to liquid-cooled IT equipment. Its electrical and control dependencies belong in the continuity review.
A rack power assembly that converts the incoming LVDC supply to an extra-low-voltage DC rack bus, with its own interface and operating requirements.
Controlled charging of downstream input capacitance before enabling a lower-impedance main path, to manage inrush and connection state.
A transient current associated with energizing equipment, such as charging initially uncharged input capacitors.
A controller that manages relevant connection, inrush and fault functions for an energized input interface. It does not imply every isolation or protective function.
The human work procedure: roles, authorization, ordered actions and required checks for an operation.
The automated operating logic defining states, permissives, transitions, timeouts and responses to abnormal conditions.
A condition that must be satisfied before the system is allowed to perform a requested action.
A verification method that exercises real control hardware against a simulated system to examine defined behaviors and exceptions.
The ability of equipment to function in its intended electromagnetic environment without causing unacceptable disturbance to other equipment.
A disturbance between the power conductors, with current returning through the associated circuit conductors.
A disturbance of conductors together relative to a shared reference, with a return path that can include chassis, earth and distributed capacitance.
Behavior over an operating region in which a reduction in input voltage is associated with increased current demand, as can occur in a regulated constant-power load.
The organization or person responsible for enforcing applicable requirements or approving equipment, materials or an installation within a defined jurisdiction.
An evaluation framework for a defined product or purpose within the relevant certification context. Check its scope and current status.
A decision that defines or clarifies requirements within a particular certification framework; confirm its scope and applicability.
A stated condition on which a proposed design or analysis relies, which must remain distinguishable from demonstrated evidence.
Records or results that address a specific claim against defined conditions and acceptance criteria.
